title: How Can You Tell If a Curriculum Truly Builds Knowledge?
author: Natalie Wexler
summary: Natalie Wexler analyzes how to distinguish true knowledge-building curricula from faux ones. Using Benchmark Advance as a case study, she reveals that curricula with broad themes and disconnected texts lack the coherence needed to build lasting knowledge. Third-party curriculum ratings systems are unreliable, and educators need better tools to evaluate actual knowledge-building effectiveness.
points: Faux coherence: texts relate thematically but don't refer to or build on each other
Decodable text restrictions prevent students from accessing complex, topic-building content
Broad themes vs. specific topics: true knowledge-building requires depth, not coverage
EdReports ratings mislead educators; Knowledge Matters Campaign list more reliable
Curriculum rating system needs improvement to prevent million-dollar district mistakes
Teachers need knowledge about reading science to evaluate curriculum quality
quotes: If kids are learning about a topic, that's 'knowledge-building' to some people.
Our current system of rating curriculum is frankly bananas.” Archived from Substack on yes by Tim.
